question: How much will Crude Oil Futures total price returns exceed S&P 500 Futures in these biweekly periods of Q4 2026? (Nov 9 - Nov 20)

calls.reasoning: Hormuz crisis regime: WTI ~$97-100 on Nov 2 after a 4-6% drop on US-Iran/Qatar peace-talk hopes; OVX 58.5 (Oct 30). Implied 2-week CL SD ~11-12%; oil-equity correlation negative in supply-shock regime widens the CL-ES spread. Median shifted negative by CL=F front-month roll (Dec->Jan around Nov 19-20) in backwardation (~-1 to -3%) plus ES drift ~+0.3. Fat tails both ways: peace deal/Hormuz reopening could crash oil >20%; talks collapse spikes it. Market check: no market prices this spread; Polymarket November WTI touch markets (<$90 ~50%, >$110 ~45%) only show traders expect a very wide range of oil prices.
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off Yahoo Finance CL=F and ES=F daily closes: P0 = close Fri Nov 6 2026, P1 = close Fri Nov 20 2026; value = CL% - ES%. Event window: Nov 6 close -> Nov 20 close; as of Nov 2 0% elapsed (window has not started).
- Context (Wikipedia 2026-2028 oil chronology): US-Israeli war on Iran, Strait of Hormuz disrupted. Aug 7 WTI $78.18; Aug 20 $86.64; Sep 9 $96.05; Sep 30 $92.16; Oct 16 $101.41 (weekly gain >10%).
- Nov 2 2026 (Reuters via wtaq.com; indiainfoline): WTI fell ~4-6% to ~$97.4-100 after Iranian-Qatari talks to end the war, and Trump extended negotiations instead of taking military action. Brent ~$106-109. S&P E-minis +0.5% the same morning. WTI up ~74% YTD.
- OVX (moomoo): 58.48 on Oct 30 2026; 51.69 on Oct 1; 52-week range 28.4-126 (peak Mar 12 2026). Implies a 2-week 1-SD CL move of ~11-12%.
- In this regime oil and equities move in opposite directions (peace news: oil down, stocks up), which widens the CL-ES spread relative to CL vol alone.
- Contract roll: CL=F is the front month. Dec 2026 CL last trade is about Nov 19-20 by my calculation, so Yahoo likely switches from Dec to Jan inside the window. With later-month prices below nearer-month prices (likely given the supply shock), the roll mechanically lowers the measured CL return by the Dec-Jan spread (rough guess 1-3%; not verified).
- Both directions: peace deal / Hormuz reopening could drop oil 20%+ (August precedent: a ~$15 drop when reopening looked imminent); talks collapse or escalation could spike it 10-20% (October precedent).
- Other events in the window: US midterms (Nov 3, before the window), ISM data, the earnings tail; ES 2-week SD ~3-4%.
- Markets: Polymarket has November WTI touch-level markets and Kalshi has WTI year-end markets; nothing prices the CL-ES spread directly.
- Searched but not found: the actual Dec-Jan CL spread, the exact Yahoo roll date, and the ES implied vol (VIX) level.

calls.reasoning: Spread dominated by crude oil in a Hormuz-crisis vol regime (OVX ~58); 1-sigma ~12pp. Median shifted negative ~-1.8 by the expected CL=F roll: the Dec contract's last trade is Fri Nov 20, so P1 may be the cheaper Jan contract in a backwardated curve (~3.5% front spread in Oct), at roughly 50-70% odds. ES drift is a small offset. Two-sided geopolitical fat tails (deal -> crash, escalation -> spike) priced as escape mass. No human market prices this spread.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on the window (Nov 6 close -> Nov 20 close), the vol regime and the roll bias, and differed only in the median (-1.5 vs -2.5) and tail mass. Factual roll timing: by CME rules the Dec 2026 CL contract's last trade is 3 business days before Nov 25 (Wed), i.e. Fri Nov 20, so a Yahoo roll inside the window is plausible but not certain; the exact Yahoo convention was unverifiable without web access, so the roll was weighted ~50-70% with a ~2.5-3.5% backwardation size, giving ~-1.5pp expected drag. I took the dispersion forward from the runs because I agree with the vol math. The median is set at -1.8 on the evidence, not by averaging.
